name: Social Security System

configuration.limitation: RA 11199 ss.4(a)(9), 8(i), 9(a) and 18; SSS Circular 2024-006 (business employers) and Circular 2024-007 (household employers), effective January 2025. Regular SS uses the first PHP20,000 monthly salary credit at 5% employee and 10% employer; excess to PHP35,000 belongs to SSS_MPF. Initial compulsory coverage extends through the 60th birthday. The first contribution liability date includes earlier employers and is independent of current registration. Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/employees/ . Separation and retirement payments outside remuneration for services are excluded. The payable missing-birth-date branch refuses assessment instead of reporting zero liability. Circular 2024-007 gives household compensation below PHP5,000 nine distinct MSC brackets from PHP1,000 to PHP5,000; the household employer pays the full 15% regular SS share, while the employee pays zero. From PHP5,000 compensation, the regular employer/employee split applies. RA 10361 s.30 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514): a domestic worker is covered by SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG after at least one month of service — `months_through(service_start, last employed day of the period)` under 1.0 charges nothing. MSC is the monthly salary credit between PHP 4,000 and PHP 35,000; 5%/10% is the 2025 regular-employer split (Circular 2024-006). RA 11199 s.9(a): compulsory coverage begins for an employee not over sixty; a member covered before sixty keeps contributing while employed — the SSS standing election `covered_before_60` (recorded default false: unrecorded, no contribution past sixty). RA 10361 s.30 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514): a domestic worker is covered after at least one month of service — `person.household_first_month` (DOMESTIC terms, under one completed month at the start of the period) charges nothing.

warn_when.message: date of birth missing: SSS treats the employee as under 60.

name: PhilHealth

configuration.limitation: Republic Act 11223 (Universal Health Care Act) s.10 with PhilHealth Circular 2020-0005 (Revision 1) (https://www.philhealth.gov.ph/circulars/2020/circ2020-0005.pdf) §V.A–C and Advisory 2025-0002 ¶1 — one 5% premium on the monthly basic salary, floor PHP 10,000, ceiling PHP 100,000, then split: employee = round(premium / 2, 0.01, 'TRUNCATE'), employer = premium - employee (PC 2020-0005 Rev.1 §V.B: “equally shared between the employee and employer”; the circular is silent on an odd centavo, so the employee half truncates and the employer carries the remainder, a recorded default; a half-centavo premium such as basic 15,819 -> 790.95 gives 395.47 / 395.48, not 395.48 twice). The base is the BASIC line, which Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keeps whole against undertime, tardiness, leave without pay and absences (the ABSENCE and NO_PAY_LEAVE lines are not subtracted). PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keys the premium off the basic monthly salary stated in the contract, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`). PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keys the premium off the basic monthly salary stated in the contract, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`). The base is the monthly basic salary whatever the pay frequency (`terms.monthly_basic`: a daily or hourly rate carried to the month by the person’s own factor). RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.30 and PC 2020-0005 Rev.1 §V.G: where a domestic worker earns less than ₱5,000 a month the employer pays the whole premium — the employee share is zero and the employer carries both. the contractual basic is read only for a month the employment touches — a settlement run after the exit month (separation pay, a 13th month settled late) has no monthly basic (PhilHealth: RA 11223 s.10, Advisory 2025-0002 ¶1, a premium on the monthly basic salary of an employed member; Pag-IBIG: RA 9679 s.7, HDMF Circular 460 pp.1-2, 2% of an employee’s monthly fund salary), so no premium is charged on it. the schedule is cited as PhilHealth Circular 2020-0005 (Revision 1), the circular PA2025-0002 ¶1 and PA2026-0042 name; the 50/50 split is §V.B. RA 10361 s.30 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514): a domestic worker is covered by SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG after at least one month of service — `months_through(service_start, last employed day of the period)` under 1.0 charges nothing. The base is the contractual monthly basic (`terms.base_salary`) whole in any month a BASIC line is paid (PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3), so a part month and unpaid absences do not reduce it. RA 10361 s.30 and PC 2020-0005 Rev.1 §V.G: a domestic worker earning less than ₱5,000 a month pays nothing and the employer pays the whole premium (`person.household_low`). RA 10361 s.30 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514): a domestic worker is covered after at least one month of service — `person.household_first_month` (DOMESTIC terms, under one completed month at the start of the period) charges nothing.

name: Pag-IBIG Fund (Home Development Mutual Fund)

configuration.limitation: Republic Act 9679 ss.6–7 and HDMF Circular 460 (15 January 2024; contributions effective February 2024), pp.1–3: monthly Fund Salary is basic salary and other allowances received in the month. Employee contribution is 1% up to PHP1,500 and 2% above PHP1,500; employer contribution is 2%, with a PHP10,000 compensation ceiling. Republic Act 10361 s.30: domestic workers are covered after at least one month of service; where monthly Fund Salary is below PHP5,000, the employer pays both shares. Contributions use remuneration actually paid for the employment month, including covered allowances and deducting unpaid absence. Sources: https://wcms.dmw.gov.ph/uploads/DMW_ADVISORY_37_2025_01225b9fec.pdf ; https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/19155 ; https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514 Coverage history: HDMF Circular 460 C.1–2 (official DMW annex pp.2–4); Circular 274 B and H.2–4 (certified ONAR copy https://naro.law.upd.edu.ph/issuances/5476, p.8). Private initial coverage not over 60 is distinct from continuing membership until compulsory Fund retirement at 65. Non-compulsory termination permits mandatory re-enrolment when coverage resumes; self-paying and voluntary classes have no automatic employer payroll counterpart. Membership facts require a recorded evidence reference; missing registration never establishes exemption. RA 10361 s.30: where a domestic worker’s monthly Fund Salary is below ₱5,000 the employer pays both shares (`person.household_low`). RA 10361 s.30 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514): a domestic worker is covered after at least one month of service — `person.household_first_month` (DOMESTIC terms, under one completed month at the start of the period) charges nothing.

name: Withholding Tax on Compensation

person.floor: terms.employment_type == "DOMESTIC" ? (company.region in rules.minimum_wage.by_employment_type.DOMESTIC && size(rules.minimum_wage.by_employment_type.DOMESTIC[company.region].filter(e, e.from <= period.to)) > 0 ? double(first(rules.minimum_wage.by_employment_type.DOMESTIC[company.region].filter(e, e.from <= period.to)).monthly) : -1.0) : (has(company.facts.bmbe_certificate_of_authority) && company.facts.bmbe_certificate_of_authority) ? -1.0 : company.region in rules.minimum_wage.by_region && size(rules.minimum_wage.by_region[company.region].filter(e, e.from <= period.to)) > 0 ? double(first(rules.minimum_wage.by_region[company.region].filter(e, e.from <= period.to)).monthly) * (has(terms.facts.days_per_year) ? double(terms.facts.days_per_year) : 313.0) / 313.0 : -1.0
person.pool_now: (year.special + month.special) + (year.bonus + month.bonus) + (year.ot_meal + month.ot_meal) + max(0.0, (year.rice + month.rice) - 2000.0 * double(period.month)) + max(0.0, (year.laundry + month.laundry) - 300.0 * double(period.month)) + max(0.0, (year.dep_medical + month.dep_medical) - 250.0 * double(period.month)) + max(0.0, (year.uniform + month.uniform) - 7000.0) + max(0.0, (year.medical + month.medical) - 10000.0) + max(0.0, (year.award + month.award) - 10000.0) + max(0.0, (year.gift + month.gift) - 5000.0) + max(0.0, (year.cba + month.cba) - 10000.0) + max(0.0, (year.leave + month.leave) - 10.0 * (terms.base_salary * 12.0 / (has(terms.facts.days_per_year) ? double(terms.facts.days_per_year) : 313.0)))
person.pool_before: year.special + year.bonus + year.ot_meal + max(0.0, year.rice - 2000.0 * (double(period.month) - 1.0)) + max(0.0, year.laundry - 300.0 * (double(period.month) - 1.0)) + max(0.0, year.dep_medical - 250.0 * (double(period.month) - 1.0)) + max(0.0, year.uniform - 7000.0) + max(0.0, year.medical - 10000.0) + max(0.0, year.award - 10000.0) + max(0.0, year.gift - 5000.0) + max(0.0, year.cba - 10000.0) + max(0.0, year.leave - 10.0 * (terms.base_salary * 12.0 / (has(terms.facts.days_per_year) ? double(terms.facts.days_per_year) : 313.0)))

configuration.assessment: max(0.0, (terms.base_salary > 0.0 && terms.base_salary <= person.floor ? 0.0 : month.wage - person.contributions) + month.ordinary + month.supplementary) + max(0.0, person.pool_now - 90000.0) - max(0.0, person.pool_before - 90000.0)

rules.employee: base.assessed <= 20833.0 ? 0.0 : base.assessed <= 33333.0 ? round((base.assessed - 20833.0) * 0.15, 0.01, "HALF_UP") : base.assessed <= 66667.0 ? round(1875.0 + (base.assessed - 33333.0) * 0.20, 0.01, "HALF_UP") : base.assessed <= 166667.0 ? round(8541.8 + (base.assessed - 66667.0) * 0.25, 0.01, "HALF_UP") : base.assessed <= 666667.0 ? round(33541.8 + (base.assessed - 166667.0) * 0.30, 0.01, "HALF_UP") : round(183541.8 + (base.assessed - 666667.0) * 0.35, 0.01, "HALF_UP")

configuration.limitation: Not modelled: the overtime/night meal exemption (the statutory context carries no overtime dates, so the whole `ot_meal` part joins the ₱90,000 pool); the year-end annualisation and refund (RR 2-98 s.2.79(B)(5)(b)); the 25% final tax on a non-resident alien not engaged in trade or business (NIRC s.25(B)); the semi-monthly, weekly and daily columns (every payslip is assessed month to date on the monthly column).

authority: NIRC s.24(A)(2)(a) as amended by RA 10963 (TRAIN) and s.79; RR 11-2018 Annex E, the monthly withholding table in force from 1 January 2023 (https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/Annex%20E%20RR%2011-2018.pdf): nothing to ₱20,833; 15% over 20,833; 1,875 + 20% over 33,333; 8,541.80 + 25% over 66,667; 33,541.80 + 30% over 166,667; 183,541.80 + 35% over 666,667. The month is assessed to date over every payslip of the month. Parts: `wage` (basic, overtime, holiday and no-pay lines), `ordinary` (other regular pay), `supplementary` (commission, RR 11-2018 s.2.79(B)(3)), `special` (13th-month pay) and `bonus`, `leave` (monetised leave) and one part per de minimis class. NIRC s.32(B)(7)(f) and RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(B)(12): the employee shares of SSS (Regular SS and MPF), PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG are excluded — `person.contributions` is the month's employee shares as charged so far (`charged.month.SSS/SSS_MPF/PHIC/HDMF.employee`, assessed before WTAX). NIRC s.32(B)(7)(e) as amended by RA 10963: 13th-month pay and other benefits are excluded to ₱90,000 a year; RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3) as amended by RR 11-2018 (and RR 4-2025 for uniforms and achievement awards, from 30 January 2025): de minimis benefits are outside compensation to their ceilings — rice ₱2,000 and laundry ₱300 a month, medical cash to dependants ₱1,500 a semester, uniform ₱7,000, actual medical assistance ₱10,000, achievement awards ₱10,000, Christmas/anniversary gifts ₱5,000 and CBA/productivity benefits ₱10,000 a year, monetised unused leave to 10 days a year, overtime/night meal to 25% of the regional basic minimum wage a day; RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3) closing paragraph: the excess over a ceiling joins the ₱90,000 pool (`person.pool_now` / `person.pool_before`, the year to date with and without this month; the month withholds on the pool's new excess). NIRC s.24(A)(2) and RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(B)(13): a minimum wage earner is exempt on the statutory minimum wage, holiday, overtime and night pay (the `wage` part) and taxed on other pay (Soriano v. Secretary of Finance, G.R. 184450, 24 January 2017); `person.floor` is the wage order's monthly floor for `company.region` in force on the period's last day in force on the period's last day in force on the period's last day (the version's PAYROLL rule `minimum_wage`, daily rate × 313 ÷ 12, restated on the contract term fact `days_per_year` factor) or the kasambahay floor; a certified BMBE (RA 9178 s.8) has no floor and its employees are taxed on the table. Recorded defaults: a region the version does not list has no floor (taxed); a monthly ceiling is read cumulatively against the months elapsed in the year; the dependants' semester ceiling is read as a sixth a month; the daily rate for the leave ceiling is the monthly basic × 12 ÷ `days_per_year` (313 when unrecorded); a minimum wage earner's contributions are not deducted (they relate to exempt pay).
